2 cash-heavy stocks with impressive fundamentals and 1 that underwhelm

Companies with more cash than debt can be financially resilient, but that doesn't mean they're all strong investments. Some lack leverage because they struggle to grow or generate consistent profits, making them unattractive borrowers.

Financial flexibility is valuable, but it's not everything - at StockStory, we help you find the stocks that can not only survive but also outperform. Keeping that in mind, here are two companies with net cash positions that can continue growing sustainably and one with hidden risks.

One stock to sell:
Marqeta (MQ)

Net Cash Position: $696.8 million (35.5% of Market Cap)

Powering the cards behind innovative fintech services like Block's Cash App, Marqeta (NASDAQ:MQ) provides a cloud-based platform that allows businesses to create customized payment card programs and process card transactions.

Why Do We Think Twice About MQ?

Revenue increased by 11% annually over the last five years, acceptable on an absolute basis but tepid for a software company enjoying secular tailwinds

Extended payback periods on sales investments suggest the company's platform isn't resonating enough to drive efficient sales conversions

Capital intensity will likely increase as its free cash flow margin is anticipated to drop by 8.9 percentage points over the next year

Marqeta's stock price of $18.86 implies a valuation ratio of 2.8x forward price-to-sales. If you're considering MQ for your portfolio, see our FREE research report to learn more.

Two stocks to buy:
Lyft (LYFT)

Net Cash Position: $619.4 million (9.7% of Market Cap)

Founded by Logan Green and John Zimmer as a long-distance intercity carpooling company Zimride, Lyft (NASDAQ: LYFT) operates a ridesharing network in the US and Canada.

Why Do We Love LYFT?

Has the opportunity to boost monetization through new features and premium offerings as its active riders have grown by 13.7% annually over the last two years

Performance over the past three years shows its incremental sales were extremely profitable, as its annual earnings per share growth of 70.4% outpaced its revenue gains

Free cash flow margin expanded by 24.8 percentage points over the last few years, providing additional flexibility for investments and share buybacks/dividends

Lyft is trading at $16.96 per share, or 7.7x forward EV/EBITDA. Is now the time to initiate a position? See for yourself in our comprehensive research report, it's free.

Tutor Perini (TPC)

Net Cash Position: $806.5 million (20% of Market Cap)

Known for constructing the Philadelphia Eagles' Stadium, Tutor Perini (NYSE:TPC) is a civil and building construction company offering diversified general contracting and design-build services.

title: Verizon Beats and Raises Guidance While Warning the FCC About SpaceX’s Phone Network
detail:
Verizon Beats and Raises Guidance While Warning the FCC About SpaceX’s Phone Network
Roxanna Maglangit

VZ

Trading disclosure
Verizon Beats and Raises Guidance While Warning the FCC About SpaceX's Phone Network ©U.S. Air Force photo by Trevor Cokley and SUMALI IBNU CHAMID from Alemedia.id via Canva
Key Takeaways

Verizon beat third-quarter profit estimates with adjusted EPS of $1.31, added 406,000 postpaid phones and raised its full-year guidance for the third straight quarter.

SpaceX's planned phone network hasn't hurt Verizon's earnings, but it is weighing on the valuation: Verizon's forward P/E has dropped to 8.8x from 10.5x in March.

Revenue of $34.31 billion missed estimates, and revenue per postpaid account fell 1.9%, which is the cost of Verizon's decision to stop raising prices.

Through their trade group, Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile asked the FCC to keep satellites off two key 5G bands ahead of an Oct. 29 vote on satellite-to-phone rules.

Verizon (VZ:NYSE) beat third-quarter profit estimates this morning and raised its full-year guidance for the third straight quarter.

Just days earlier, Verizon, AT&T (T:NYSE) and T-Mobile had joined their trade group in lobbying the FCC on satellite-to-phone rules. That matters because SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) is planning a phone network of its own for 2028.

So far, the only place SpaceX hurts Verizon is the stock price. (Shares fell [2%] today, even after the beat.)

TIKR tracks 25 analysts on Verizon. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Verizon, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Verizon's Analyst Ratings

What exactly happened

Verizon's third-quarter results were strong almost everywhere that counts…

Adjusted EPS of $1.31, above the $1.28 analysts expected

406,000 postpaid phone net adds, its best third quarter in five years, plus 137,000 net new postpaid accounts, its best in over a decade

Consumer postpaid phone churn of 0.87%, down from 0.91% a year earlier

Adjusted EBITDA of $13.8 billion, up 8% and a company record

Free cash flow of $7.8 billion, up 12.1%

Management now expects 2026 adjusted EPS of $5.04 to $5.06, or 7% to 7.5% growth, up from 6% to 7% before. It also expects 1.1 million to 1.2 million postpaid phone net adds this year. The old target was the upper half of 750,000 to 1 million.

Revenue was the one miss. It came in at $34.31 billion, up 1.5% but below the $34.77 billion consensus. Revenue per postpaid account fell 1.9% to $168.08.

Verizon chose that trade. It stopped pushing through yearly price increases so fewer customers would leave. Back in January, management said the change would cost about 1.8 percentage points of service revenue growth this year.

And Verizon doesn't have much room to give up. Revenue went from $134 billion in fiscal 2021 to $138 billion in fiscal 2025, barely any growth in five years.

title: What Just Happened To T-Mobile Stock?
detail:
What Just Happened To T-Mobile Stock?
Trefis Team

T-Mobile US (TMUS) shares fell 7.7% on Friday, October 23, 2026, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.5%. The company did not report earnings that day. Instead, news reports linked the fall to a report that SpaceX is seeking at least 80,000 U.S. cell sites to build a fourth nationwide wireless carrier. That carrier is only a plan for now, so why did it weigh on T-Mobile on Friday?

How SpaceX Could Compete With T-Mobile

According to news reports, the plan raised the prospect of fierce competition between SpaceX and the industry's big three carriers. SpaceX bought extra cellphone spectrum for its satellites earlier in October 2026, news reports said, and the company now wants to lease ground cell towers.

Such a rival could compete for the monthly bill-paying customers that T-Mobile has relied upon for growth. On the July 23, 2026 call, management said postpaid service revenue rose 13% in the second quarter.

Did T-Mobile Fall With Other Carriers?

Yes, although not all of them fell as hard. AT&T dropped 8.0%, falling about as much as T-Mobile, while Verizon lost 1.2%. Four of the five companies in T-Mobile's Trefis peer group ended the day lower, and the SPDR fund for the communication services sector, XLC, fell 1.8%. T-Mobile fell alongside most of its peers, but only AT&T dropped as far.

Where Does T-Mobile Stock Stand Now?

A fall this large is not new for T-Mobile. Over the prior 365 days, the stock recorded two sessions with a drop at least this big, the latest being a 13.3% fall on October 9, 2026.

If you bought T-Mobile on October 22, 2025, you are down 34.2% including dividends, while the S&P 500 returned 15.1%. The slide has continued lately, with the shares losing 16.8% from July 27 to October 23, 2026, while the index gained 3.1%. Friday's close of $146.54 was the stock's lowest in a year. Since October 23, 2025, its highest close was $221.98 on February 24, 2026.

At that price, T-Mobile trades at 1.7 times its sales over the last twelve months, compared with 3.2 times for the S&P 500.

T-Mobile reports its third-quarter results later in October 2026. Management expected net postpaid account additions of about 250,000 for that quarter, held back by a temporary rise in account churn from its rate plan modernization. That figure is the number to watch in the report.

AT&T (T) shares fell 8.0% on Friday, October 23, 2026, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.5%. News reports that day linked the drop to a report that SpaceX wants access to at least 80,000 cell sites across the U.S. T-Mobile US fell 7.7% in the same session. What ties SpaceX's plans to AT&T's shares, two days after AT&T's own results?

Why A SpaceX Report Hit AT&T Stock

News reports said the prospect of SpaceX gaining access to that many cell sites was stoking competition fears for wireless carriers, including AT&T. The company's wireless business was growing when it posted third-quarter results on October 21. Wireless service revenues rose 5% from a year earlier. During the period, AT&T added a net 379,000 postpaid phone customers, which are subscribers who pay a monthly bill.

AT&T beat estimates for both earnings and revenue in the quarter. Adjusted earnings per share were $0.65, against an estimate of $0.60, and revenue was $32.3 billion, against the $31.7 billion expected. Management also raised its full-year outlook for adjusted earnings per share to about $2.40, from a prior range of $2.25 to $2.35. AT&T stock fell 6.4% on the day of the report.

During the October 21 call, management was asked about satellites providing mobile service. It said that reaching the performance customers have come to expect from today's large networks takes a lot of years and a huge level of investment.

AT&T Fell Alongside T-Mobile US

T-Mobile US shared in the drop, while the rest of AT&T's peer list and its sector moved far less. Verizon Communications fell 1.2% in the same session, and four of AT&T's five peers fell. The SPDR fund for its sector, XLC, lost 1.8%.

Where AT&T Stock Stands After The Drop

Falls this large are rare for AT&T, but this was the second one in October. Over the prior 365 days, only one session recorded a fall at least this large: October 9, when the stock dropped 9.8%.

AT&T stock has lost 14.2% over the past year, while the S&P 500 returned 15.1%. These losses materialized quickly, with the stock falling 16.8% in the month to October 23, against a 1.0% dip for the S&P 500. AT&T closed at $20.93, sitting just above its lowest close of the past year, which was $20.48 on July 1, 2026. The stock reached its highest close in that time on March 27, at $29.10.

The shares trade at 1.1 times AT&T's sales over the past twelve months, against 3.2 times for the S&P 500. AT&T is expected to report its fourth-quarter 2026 results in January 2027, and the net number of postpaid phone customers it adds is the measure to watch.

What Could Surprise Comcast Stock Investors On The Upside?

For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Comcast (CMCSA) stock closed on October 23, 2026, 27.3% below its highest close of the past year. The company lost 144,000 broadband subscribers in its third quarter. Trading at 7.1 times earnings, compared with 22.9 for the S&P 500, the stock price appears to assume those losses go on. Yet one business inside Comcast's home connectivity arm kept growing through that quarter. Which business is it, and how far has it come?

Comcast Keeps Adding Wireless Lines

That growing business is wireless phone service, which management says is built on Comcast's existing broadband customer base. The company ended the third quarter of fiscal 2026 with 10.6 million wireless lines, up 18% from a year earlier. Wireless service revenue grew nearly 15% in the quarter, while convergence revenue, representing Comcast's combined broadband and wireless revenue, fell 2%.

Customers are also choosing pricier plans. Premium unlimited plans made up about 40% of Comcast's postpaid phone connects in the quarter, up from 30% the quarter before. On its October 22, 2026, call, management called mobile "a tremendous growth opportunity" and described it as a capital-light model.

How Big Could Comcast's Wireless Business Get?

Management said wireless has reached nearly 18% penetration of Comcast's residential broadband base. Those lines also make up only about 7% of the total wireless lines Comcast could address in the areas its network covers, a figure management described on the call as huge upside.

Wireless is not yet big enough to lift Comcast's home business. It sits inside Residential Connectivity & Platforms, which brought in $70.7 billion in fiscal 2025, down 1.2% from a year earlier. Management said third-quarter wireless growth only partly offset continued pressure on broadband revenue.

So far, the stock has lagged the market. Comcast stock lost 13.4% over the year to October 23, 2026, including dividends, while the S&P 500 returned 15.1%.

What Must Go Right For Comcast In Wireless?

Comcast has to turn free lines into paying customers. About half of its residential postpaid phone connects in the third quarter came from customers taking a free line. Management said the company now converts 70% of those free lines into paying relationships.

The market is also crowded. On the October 22 call, management said that wireless remains competitive, and that customers switched providers a little less often in the quarter as new combined offers reached the market.
